source_text: Cost-utility analyses yield mixed results, with some U.S.-focused models estimating lifetime savings from reduced STI/UTI treatments (e.g., $407 increased costs per male if circumcision rates drop to 10%), though these assume high efficacy and discount rates favoring early intervention; critics argue they undervalue procedural risks and overstate rare-event prevention in modern contexts with vaccination and screening.
